newsitem.title: UK: Retailers call for meter charge inquiry - paper.
newsitem.headline: Retailers call for meter charge inquiry - paper.

text.p: UK retailers are set to call for an inquiry into the electricity industry's rising meter charges, a report in The Times said on Friday.
The report said the British Retail Consortium is to weigh in with its criticisms, joining electricity customers, including supermarket J Sainsbury Plc and the Royal Mail.
The Consortium, which represents 90 percent of retail stores, will demand an end to "unregulated and arbitrary" charges for commerical companies' electricity bills, it said.
The group will now ask the electricity regulator, Offer, to intervene, accusing the pricing system of the so-called electricity pool of being non-transparent and unaccountable.
The commercial customer meter charge rose to 565 stg per meter this year from 299 stg, prompting some clients to delay payment of part of their bill in protest.

James May, director general of the Consortium, was quoted in The Times saying: "These annual charges have infuriated many of our larger members." But a spokesman for the electricity pool was quoted responding: "The pool's charge on suppliers pays the annual costs of operating the 100 kilowatt competitive market with customers gaining significant and sustained price reductions since the market's introduction in 1994." -- London newsroom +44 171 5427717
